title: Use arrow functions in connector types to fix `@typescript-eslint/no-unbound-method` errors
body: **Summary** Currently, the `RenderState` types for connectors inconsistently declare functions as either arrow functions or regular functions: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/3faca014aad08145c3b4cc66a5e841da3a0f64b8/src/connectors/search-box/connectSearchBox.ts#L41 https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/74d98f1fcd0d3560c63e4e4dc6dfaa848eb7f5bb/src/connectors/refinement-list/connectRefinementList.ts#L111 In user code, the latter leads to spurious lint errors from the [`@typescript-eslint/no-unbound-method` lint rule](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/unbound-method.md) when trying to assign the property to a standalone variable. For example, destructuring the return value of the `useRefinementList` hook [as shown in the Algolia docs](https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-reference/widgets/refinement-list/react-hooks/#hook) results in this lint error: I did a rudimentary regex search of the connector functions to find other affected type declarations, but may have missed some. **Result** Lint error goes away after building and `link`ing this branch.

Is it expected that you see eslint errors for library code? Shouldn't node_modules be ignored?
If it makes sense to enforce a specific style, we should enable https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/method-signature-style.md

The lint rule doesn't run on internal library code, but it does look at the _exported_ library types, since it can be used to help detect invalid library usage. These connector types get exported in the public API so they end up affecting the lint errors.


> If it makes sense to enforce a specific style, we should enable [https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/method-signature-style.md](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/main/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/method-signature-style.md?rgh-link-date=2022-05-30T08%3A52%3A35Z)

That's a good idea. One downside is that it looks like the InstantSearch.js library _does_ rely on `this` in certain places, so there are some function types where the non-arrow function might be more accurate. It doesn't change the runtime behavior though, so it's probably not a big deal.
I'm happy to accept a PR that changes all to arrow functions, and then also add the no-unbound-method rule here. Would you be interested in continuing?
Sure! I'll push an update later to make those changes.
I'll close this for now, but happy to collaborate if you want to revisit this
